title: Kid Rena and comparing favourite trumpeters
summary: Howard praises Rena's big, clean tone and again names Chris Kelly and Armstrong as favourites.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: I was wondering if he played much like at the time that you went to Chicago, was he still active as a musician then? Yeah. Still working? Yeah. Yeah. Well 1930, even by Buddy McKee's death, he was still? Yeah, he was playing. Still playing. Mm-hmm. I'm going to ask a little bit about Kid Rene, if you heard him very much, how he played. I even met him and heard him play, but he was not very well when I heard him. Well when you heard him, he was shot up then.
Yeah. But he was wonderful. He was really good. Yeah, really good. I was Paul Barrett for a year when he died.
Now did you ever play with him in any brass bands? Yeah.
Yeah, I played brass bands with him.
Was he mostly high note bands on people of Tony?
Yeah, he could go up there. Clean. Clean, what?
Was it a big tone or sort of small tone? No, no, big tone.
Big tone. Big tone, yeah. A wonderful trumpet man. Clean. Yeah. Could do that.
Do you still prefer Chris Kelly to Buddy McKee and Kid Rene and those other men, Sam Marginal and D. Yeah, Lewis and Chris. And Chris are the two idols favorites. That's mine.
They're wonderful. Very tough. But I like Chris with that mule. Like that.
